nodes.action: ran the migration during peak traffic
the lockout cascaded to every dependent service
ran the migration in a maintenance window
the migration finished without locking anything
configured a read-replica failover so services kept running during locks
ran the deployment during peak hours
switched to online schema migration since maintenance windows still caused locks

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Morning, Kim. You look like you've been up since 3 AM.

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.text: Because I have. That migration you ran yesterday? During peak traffic? The database locked up hard.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Yeah, I know. I thought it would be fine — we'd done dry runs. But the lock cascaded to every dependent service. Checkout, inventory, even the search autocomplete went down.

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.text: We had customers tweeting about it. I had to manually restart three queues. What were you thinking?

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: I was thinking we needed to get it done before the quarter close. But you're right — that was a mistake. I'll schedule it in a maintenance window next time.

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.text: A maintenance window is better, but we still need to be careful. The lock itself is the problem, not just when we run it.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: I hear you. I'll set up a proper window for the next one, and I'll also look into a read-replica failover so services can keep running even if a lock happens.

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.text: That would be a huge improvement. Let's talk after you've got a plan.

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.text: Hey, I saw you ran the migration again last night. How did it go?

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Smooth. I ran it in a maintenance window at 2 AM, and I configured a read-replica failover beforehand. Even if it had locked, the app would have kept serving reads from the replica.

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.text: Nice. So no lock at all?

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: No lock. The migration finished without locking anything. It was almost boring.

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.text: Boring is good. But I noticed you also deployed the new payment service during peak hours yesterday — and that caused an outage.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Ugh, yeah. That was a separate mistake. I thought the deployment was low-risk, but it took down the API gateway for 20 minutes.

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.text: We need to stop doing this to ourselves. Can you schedule deployments for off-peak hours from now on?

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Absolutely. I've already set up a deployment calendar — everything goes out between 1 AM and 4 AM. No more peak-hour releases.

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.text: Good. Let's see if we can get a few clean releases in a row.

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.text: Hey, I saw the last two releases went out without incidents. Nice work.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Thanks. Off-peak scheduling plus the read-replica failover has been solid. But I need to tell you something about the maintenance window approach.

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.text: What do you mean?

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Turns out that wasn't enough. Even in a maintenance window, the migration still locks the database — it just locks it when fewer people are around. But we still get lock waits, and if anything goes wrong, we're stuck.

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.text: So you're saying the maintenance window was a band-aid?

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Exactly. I was wrong about it being a real fix. So I switched to online schema migration — we're using gh-ost now. It runs in chunks, doesn't take a full lock, and the app stays fully available.

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.text: That's a big change. How did the last migration go with that?

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Flawless. No lock, no downtime, and we didn't even need the maintenance window. We just ran it during normal hours.

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.text: That's the right call. I'm glad you didn't just settle for the window.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Me too. Lesson learned — the real fix is to not lock at all, not just to lock at a quieter time.
